newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe hits back at Jospin on finances.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe hits back at Jospin on finances.

text.p: Defeated French conservative ex-prime minister Alain Juppe hit back at his Socialist successor Lionel Jospin on Thursday, disputing charges that public deficits were in a worse situation than he had admitted.

Aides to Juppe, in a statement faxed to reporters, said the former premier had handed Jospin a detailed note at their brief handover on June 4 showing that the economy and public finances were improving.

They said the note "shows that meeting the objectives set for 1997 and 1998 is within our reach as long as the recovery programme begun two years ago is continued and consolidated, especially the control of public spending, a decisive condition for durable, sustained growth".
The aides gave no figures but said the note contained a breakdown of the current situation of the state budget and welfare accounts.

"In this context, any increase in public spending and any interruption in the privatisation process can only make more hazardous respecting the commitments renewed in Amsterdam to enable France to qualify for European economic and monetary union," the statement from "sources close to Juppe" said.
Jospin earlier told parliament he was delaying a mini-budget and other economic policy measures until after an independent audit reports in mid-July reports on the true state of public finances.
"The first indications I have received lead me to believe that the situation of our public finances is serious," he said.
